newsitem.title: USA: Judge excuses potential juror in Oklahoma case.
newsitem.headline: Judge excuses potential juror in Oklahoma case.

text.p: Federal judge Richard Matsch on Tuesday excused a potential juror from serving in the Oklahoma City bombing trial, saying he did not believe she could be impartial.

The woman, a German-born naturalised U.S. citizen, had written in a questionnaire that she disagreed with Matsch's decision to move the trial from Oklahoma to Denver to ensure defendant Timothy McVeigh a fair hearing.

The juror was the second of the 38 potential jurors questioned so far to be immediately and publicly excused from jury duty in the trial of McVeigh, who is accused of bombing the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in 1995, killing 168 people.
A woman was dismissed last week after she disclosed that she had been treated for stress and feared breaking down under the pressure of a long trial.

The woman excused Tuesday came to the United States in 1957 after marrying an American soldier. In a questionnaire filled out last month, she wrote that she strongly disagreed with moving the trial to Denver and thought the U.S. legal system was too protective of defendants.

Matsch questioned the woman briefly, gave her a lecture on a defendant's right to a fair trial and then called prosecutors and defence attorneys to the bench for a private conference. After the morning break, the judge announced the juror had been excused mainly because of the answers she gave in the questionnaire.
